summary: Enterprise Suite AC-19 adds a review-only listener/gateway foundation for later Oyatie cloud ingress. The plan composes the 19-route local runtime catalog, 19-route auth policy, and cloud deployment manifest into a Kubernetes ClusterIP Service + Gateway API HTTPRoute contract with TLS, network-policy, authorization, route-scope, probe, timeout, backend-port, and no-direct-public-NodePort/LoadBalancer requirements. Cloud readiness consumes the plan while deployed listener runtime evidence, Gateway controller attachment, load balancer provisioning, TLS certificate attachment, runtime auth middleware, cloud deployment evidence, SLO evidence, and runtime audit-chain emission remain blockers/non-claims.

findings: The crate is a deterministic declarative plan and manifest renderer with no socket binding, Kubernetes client, controller watch, or network side effect.
Validation rejects duplicate routes, auth-policy drift, public exposure overclaims, runtime attachment flags, invalid probes, ports, hosts, and timeouts.
The slice narrows the broad deployed-listener blocker into a tested pre-cloud gateway contract plus a remaining runtime-evidence blocker.
Gateway API, TLS, network-policy, authz, and ClusterIP-only exposure are required before a future controller/load-balancer slice can claim cloud ingress.
Positive plan coverage and negative route/auth/public-ingress/runtime-overclaim paths are covered.
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if route/auth coverage, public exposure refusal, runtime-overclaim guards, host/port/probe/timeout validation, or review-only manifest rendering are weakened.

findings: Developers can call enterprise_suite_listener_gateway_plan(), validate_enterprise_suite_listener_gateway_plan(), and render_enterprise_suite_listener_gateway_review_manifest() to inspect cloud-ingress preconditions without running infrastructure.

Targeted listener/gateway check/test/clippy, cloud-readiness test/clippy, 39-package enterprise regression test/clippy, fmt, jq, data_class scan, quality-marker scan, dependency-seam gate, Oya VCS lifecycle, and audit-chain append-only checks are required for closeout.

alternatives_named: start a live Hyper listener now
add Kubernetes YAML without route/auth validation
add a typed review-only listener/gateway plan first
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The typed review-only plan makes route coverage, auth policy alignment, service exposure, and gateway controls mechanically testable before claiming runtime or cloud ingress.
rejected_reasons: A live listener would overclaim deployed runtime behavior and require auth middleware, secrets, and operational evidence not yet present.
Static YAML alone would not prove coverage against the local route catalog and auth policy.

findings: The plan requires authorization and deny-by-default policy coverage for all local routes and rejects required-scope drift.
Direct public NodePort and direct public LoadBalancer exposure are forbidden; service exposure is ClusterIP-only behind Gateway API policy.
Runtime auth middleware, TLS certificate, load balancer, controller attachment, and runtime audit emission are explicit non-claims.

findings.summary: The plan adds no runtime request cost until a future listener/controller slice attaches it.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Validation checks 19 in-memory route specs plus 19 auth policies and renders static review-only YAML; no listener, network, Kubernetes, TLS, or hot request path exists.

findings: All new public struct fields in changed source carry data_class annotations.

The design follows official Kubernetes service/gateway guidance by modeling Service exposure separately from Gateway API HTTPRoute routing and by keeping controller/load-balancer status as future runtime evidence.
Probe paths remain explicit and cloud readiness stays false until deployed listener and SLO evidence land.

The change is additive: one crate, one catalog row, workspace/dependency wiring, spec/task/evidence updates, and readiness-gate composition. No cluster, DNS, certificate, listener, load balancer, or external resource is created.

The readiness report now exposes listener_gateway_plan_ready, listener_gateway_plan_attached, listener_runtime_attached, gateway_controller_attached, load_balancer_attached, and tls_certificate_attached for later dashboards.
The deployed-listener blocker is narrowed to deployed_listener_runtime_evidence_missing to avoid confusing review-only planning with runtime ingress.
Enterprise Suite AC-19 records the staged migration boundary from local runtime composition to review-only Gateway API/Service plan and later deployed listener/controller evidence.
AC-15 cloud-readiness composition now includes listener/gateway plan readiness while still refusing cloud deployment claims.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: A listener/gateway plan improves cloud readiness only if it refuses to claim deployed listener, Gateway controller, load balancer, TLS certificate, runtime auth middleware, or cloud/SLO evidence.
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Later cloud ingress work would need to infer route, auth, probe, timeout, and exposure requirements from separate runtime/auth/deployment crates rather than a typed edge contract.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: The existing runtime adapter owns dispatch logic and the deployment manifest owns container/GitOps metadata; a separate listener-gateway plan preserves no-runtime-attachment claims while joining those surfaces.

findings: This is the next cloud-integration step after auth runtime and Postgres/RLS planning: edge exposure is now typed before any live listener or Gateway controller is attached.
Names use listener-gateway-plan/foundation vocabulary and avoid deployed gateway, live ingress, or cloud-ready claims.
Enterprise Suite spec, plan, task list, catalog, multispectrum evidence, VCS evidence, and audit-chain references are part of the closeout set.
The crate sits under microservices/enterprise-suite/crates with an infrastructure/control catalog row and only local workspace dependencies.
No listener, Kubernetes client, Gateway controller, load balancer, TLS certificate, runtime middleware, provider SDK, Workflow engine/broker, statutory rail, or runtime audit emitter was introduced.
The new listener/gateway crate has no third-party dependencies; it composes only local enterprise-suite auth, deployment-manifest, and local-runtime-composition crates.
No external wire API schema changes; the addition is a Rust control-plane/listener-gateway plan plus Enterprise Suite AC-19 metadata.
Validation and manifest rendering are deterministic checks over fixed route/auth/deployment metadata with no clock, randomness, I/O, network, or Kubernetes API calls.
